name: Trischettn
summary: South Tyrolean two-to-four player trick-taking game related to Tresette, played with a 32-card German-suited pack.
rules_text: Two-player base: remove Sixes from Salzburg pattern to make 32 cards. No trumps. Rank per suit: 10 high, then 9, Ace, King, Ober, Unter, 8, 7. Deal 8 each, remaining 16 as talon. Must follow suit if able; highest of led suit wins trick. Winner draws from talon, then opponent draws, winner leads next. After talon empty play out hand. Card points: Ace=1, Ten/Nine/King/Ober/Unter=1/3 each, last trick=1. Fractions rounded down after summing, so 11 points per deal without bonuses. Declarations score bonus when on lead after winning a trick: three Tens/Nines/Aces=3, four=4, Napoli=Ten+Nine+Ace of same suit=3. Cards can be reused in multiple declarations. Play to 31 points, sometimes 41. For 3 players deal 10 each discard 2, otherwise same. For 4 deal 8 each, declarations only on first trick, partnership signaling gestures allowed.
rating_reason: Two-player Tresette variant, trick-taking with declarations, text-only.
